core_step: Extract key frames from /root/super-mario.mp4 into /root/keyframes_%03d.png using ffmpeg
why_essential: Key frames are the input images required for all subsequent image processing and object counting steps.

core_step: Verify the extracted keyframe files and their names (ls /root/keyframes_*.png | sort)
why_essential: Confirming the extracted file list and names ensures the correct frames will be processed and enumerated in the CSV.

core_step: Convert each keyframe image to grayscale inplace using ImageMagick (convert "$i" -colorspace Gray "$i")
why_essential: The task requires frames to be overwritten as grayscale images before running template-based object counting.
evidence: for i in /root/keyframes_*.png; do convert "$i" -colorspace Gray "$i"; done && echo "Done"

core_step: Count coins, enemies, and turtles in each keyframe using the object_counter script against templates /root/coin.png, /root/enemy.png, /root/turtle.png
why_essential: Counting objects per frame is the core analytic goal; these counts populate the CSV output.
evidence: for frame in /root/keyframes_00{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8}.png; do coins=$(python3 /logs/agent/.../count_objects.py --tool count --input_...); done

core_step: Write the CSV summary file /root/counting_results.csv with columns frame_id,coins,enemies,turtles and the per-frame counts
why_essential: Producing the specified CSV file finalizes the task by saving the required summary of counts in the required location.
